newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, but in need of a kick.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, but in need of a kick.

text.p: Singapore shares crept up on low volumes on Friday with dealers in search of something to kick start the market and lift activity ahead of the new year.
"There's nothing to kick the market; people are not inclined to invest," one dealer said.
Just 34.9 million shares were moved in dull post-Christmas, pre-weekend trade, but it was enough to see the key Straits Times Industrials Index end up 4.91 points at 2,202.60.
Other indices, the UOB over-the-counter index and the Business Times-Singapore Regional Index also nudged higher, up 1.20 at 1,196.35 and 1.38 at 1,093.10 respectively.
Dealers said a lack of liquidity in the market had combined with an extended festive period to restrain trade.
"People have taken a very long break. Some fund managers are around but they're not inclined to make any big bets," a dealer said.
Friday's biggest gainer was Creative Technology, up Singapore $0.60 (US$0.43) to S$13.40, followed by port services firm China Merchants, up Hong Kong $0.60 to HK$5.10.
Losers were led by Keppel Corp warrants, down S$0.32 to S$2.36. Overall, gainers outstripped losers 195 to 98.
